property_summary: Only the owner can successfully send Ether through sendTo; the buggy version allows anyone to send, changing c's balance after a non-owner call.

For any caller and any amount up to c's balance, a successful sendTo must transfer exactly amount from c to receiver, leaving c's balance reduced by amount; the buggy version allows non-owner calls to succeed, violating the invariant that only owner can reduce c's balance.
Any non-owner caller attempting to send Ether via sendTo must result in a revert; the buggy version allows the call to succeed, violating the owner-only restriction.
For any caller and any non-zero amount, if sendTo succeeds then the caller must be the owner; the mutant breaks this by allowing non-owners to succeed.

For any caller and any amount, after a successful sendTo, the caller's balance decreases by exactly the amount sent to receiver; the buggy version breaks this by allowing non-owners to send without transferring from their own balance.
For any call to sendTo by the owner, the receiver's ETH balance must increase by the sent amount; the mutant sends to the owner instead and fails this for every non-owner receiver.

For any call to sendTo by the owner, the contract's ETH balance must decrease by the sent amount; the mutant never decreases the contract's balance and thus violates this rule for any non-zero transfer.

After any owner call to sendTo, the receiver's ETH balance must increase by exactly the amount sent; the mutant sends the funds to the owner instead, so any receiver other than the owner gets nothing.

After an owner call to sendTo, the contract's ETH balance must not increase; the mutant deposits funds to owner (which may be the contract) but never withdraws from C, so the contract balance never decreases, violating this rule when the owner is the contract itself.

For any owner call to sendTo where the receiver is not the owner and amount is positive, the receiver's ETH balance must increase by exactly the amount; the mutant sends funds to the owner instead, so a non-owner receiver's balance never increases.
After sendTo is called by the owner, the contract's Ether balance must decrease by exactly the sent amount; the buggy version never sends funds, so the balance remains unchanged.

For any owner call, a successful sendTo must reduce the contract's Ether balance by exactly the transferred amount relative to its pre-call balance; the buggy version does not transfer Ether, so the balance stays the same while the caller's balance is reduced by 0, breaking the invariant.

For any owner call with amount ≤ contract balance, if the receiver is a contract that fails on receiving Ether (causing transfer to revert), the sendTo call reverts and c's balance remains unchanged; the buggy version succeeds despite no transfer, leaving c's balance unchanged but not reverting, so the revert behavior differs.

After the owner calls sendTo, either the call reverts (due to a failing receiver) or the receiver's ETH balance increases by exactly the sent amount; the buggy version never transfers ETH, so a non-reverting call fails to increase the receiver's balance.

For any owner call, the call to sendTo must revert if and only if the internal transfer to receiver fails; the buggy version does not revert even when the receiver is a contract that cannot accept Ether.

After sendTo, the owner's ether balance in the contract must never decrease unless msg.sender is the owner; the mutant allows an attacker to drain the contract's balance by moving the transfer before the require.

After any call to sendTo, if msg.sender is not the owner, the contract's Ether balance must remain unchanged; the buggy version violates this by transferring Ether before checking ownership, allowing non-owners to drain the balance.
For any call to sendTo, if msg.sender is not the owner, the call must revert; the mutant moves the transfer before the require, allowing non-owners to successfully send Ether without reverting.

After a successful sendTo call, the contract balance must equal the previous balance minus the amount only when msg.sender is the owner; the mutant allows any sender to decrease the balance because the transfer occurs before the require, causing a state difference where the balance decreases for non-owners while the reference reverts.
For any call to sendTo, if msg.sender is not the owner, the transaction must always revert; the mutant moves the transfer before the require, allowing a non-owner to transfer Ether without reverting.
After any call to sendTo, the contract's ether balance must decrease by exactly the amount sent for the owner, but the buggy version leaves the balance unchanged.
After the owner calls sendTo, the external receiver's balance must increase by the transferred amount; the bug breaks this by skipping the transfer, so the receiver's balance remains unchanged.

After a call to sendTo by the owner, the contract's ether balance and the receiver's balance should remain unchanged regardless of the amount parameter, because the constructor never funds the contract and no other payable functions exist; the reference never has ether to transfer so transfer would revert, but the buggy version would silently succeed, changing the revert behavior.
After any successful call to sendTo, the receiver's ether balance must increase by the amount parameter, which the buggy version violates by skipping the transfer.

After a call to sendTo by the owner, the contract's ether balance must decrease by the amount sent if the transfer succeeds; the buggy version skips the transfer, so the contract balance never decreases, violating this rule even when sufficient contract balance exists.

Only the contract owner can successfully transfer ETH to a receiver; after any call to sendTo, the owner balance remains unchanged for calls by non-owners in the reference, but the bug allows non-owners to transfer ETH.

For any caller, after a call to sendTo, the contract's own ETH balance either stays the same (if caller is not owner in reference, or if receiver reverts) or decreases by the amount sent; the bug allows non-owners to drain the contract's balance beyond what the owner would allow, violating the invariant that only the owner's calls can decrease the contract balance.
A call to sendTo from a non-owner cannot reduce the contract's ETH balance in the reference, but the bug allows any caller to drain it.
A call to sendTo that does not revert must leave the contract's ETH balance unchanged if the caller is not the owner; the bug allows non-owners to reduce the contract balance.
For any caller, if sendTo succeeds (does not revert), the caller must be the owner; the bug allows non-owners to call sendTo without revert.
Only the contract owner can successfully transfer ETH via sendTo; the mutant inverts the check allowing any non-owner to succeed, which violates the invariant that non-owner calls always revert.
For any caller and any receiver and amount, a call to sendTo reverts unless the caller is the owner; the buggy version always reverts, so a call from the owner (who should succeed) instead fails.

For any caller that is the owner, any admissible receiver, and any positive amount <= owner's balance that does not cause the receiver's fallback to revert, the call succeeds (does not revert); the bug always reverts even for the owner.

For the owner caller, any receiver that does not revert on payment, and any amount > 0 and <= owner's balance, sendTo must succeed (not revert); the buggy require(msg.sender == address(0)) causes even the owner's call to always revert.

For calls from the owner with any amount to any receiver that does not impede the transfer, sendTo succeeds and reduces the contract's balance by the amount; the buggy version always reverts because it checks msg.sender == address(0).

For the owner caller and any receiver that does not revert on payment, a sendTo call with amount > 0 and less than or equal to the contract's current balance must not revert and must decrease the contract's balance by exactly the amount sent; the buggy version always reverts for the owner.
sendTo should always succeed when called by the owner, but the mutant allows only the receiver to call it, causing owner calls to revert.
A call to sendTo from an address that is neither the owner nor the receiver must revert, but the mutant allows it when msg.sender equals receiver.

For any sender and any receiver, a call to sendTo(receiver, amount) must succeed (not revert) if and only if msg.sender is the owner; the buggy version succeeds when msg.sender is the receiver, violating this equivalence.

After any successful call to sendTo, the contract's balance must equal the initial balance minus the amount sent; the mutant breaks this by allowing the receiver to call sendTo, causing a transfer that does not decrease the contract's balance because the receiver sends their own Ether.
Any call to sendTo from a non-owner must revert; the reference enforces this, the bug allows non-owner transfers.

For any sender and amount, the owner's balance of the C contract must remain unchanged after a call to sendTo from anyone other than the owner, which the reference enforces via the require and the bug breaks by allowing transfers from non-owners.
After any call to sendTo, the ETH balance of the contract C equals its balance before the call, because only the owner can trigger transfers and the bug removes this restriction.

For any caller and any receiver that reverts on receiving ETH, the reference C always reverts, while the buggy version sends ETH and loses it, violating the invariant that the contract's ETH balance remains unchanged when a transfer to a reverting receiver is attempted.
For any sender that is not the owner and any amount, the reference C always reverts on sendTo (preserving its ETH balance), while the buggy version succeeds, decreasing C's ETH balance.
Ether can only be transferred by the contract owner; the bug allows anyone to transfer Ether by bypassing the ownership check.
After any sequence of calls to sendTo where the caller is not the owner, the contract's Ether balance must remain unchanged; the bug allows a non-owner to drain Ether.
For any non-owner caller, sendTo must revert; the buggy check 'require(true)' never reverts, allowing non-owners to execute the transfer.
For any caller and any amount, if the caller is not the owner, the Ether balance of the contract must remain unchanged; the bug allows a non-owner to drain Ether.
For any non-owner caller sending Ether through sendTo, the call must revert; the bug replaces the ownership check with true, allowing a non-owner to execute the transfer without revert.
After any call to sendTo, the owner's balance remains unchanged; the buggy version incorrectly sends funds to the owner, increasing the owner's balance.
For any call to sendTo, the contract's Ether balance decreases by exactly the amount sent; the buggy version sends to the owner, so the contract's balance remains unchanged.
For any initial owner ether balance, after a sendTo call by the owner, the owner's ether balance remains unchanged from its pre-call value; the buggy version increases it.
For any admissible input, the receiver's balance increases by the amount and the owner's balance is unchanged; the bug sends to the owner, increasing the owner's balance and not the receiver's.
For any call to sendTo, the owner's Ether balance never exceeds its initial Ether balance; the buggy version sends funds to the owner, so the owner's balance increases.
